What matters for a beginner is damping: after a new note sounds, the same hand must immediately stop the previous one; if needed the mallets can be held at an angle, one damping one key while the other strikes the next, or there can be a short pause. Some line-ups use two sizes, barung and panerus; in the Surakarta gamelan the panerus plays a single-line melody, the barung a slower and more complex one, and gives the cue for changes when there is no rebab.

Its range is usually a little more than two octaves, with five notes to the octave; in the seven-note pélog scale some pitches are left out according to the pathet. Like the Balinese gangsa it has an individual resonator for each key; it differs from the saron, which resonates through a trough, and is higher than the slenthem, which has a lower range and fewer keys. The panerus is an octave above the barung, whose melody is slower and more complex.
